rows.notes: The catalog is addressed by category-suffixed asset name (:93), filtered by a whole-frame regex match (:108-118) and reduced to three columns unless extras are requested (:100-105,:122-128), with an optional codes asset attached as result metadata (:140-146); the sibling asset loader parses tab-delimited text (utils/helpers.py:231-237) but open_asset itself sits past the lines read, so local-versus-FTP transport is unconfirmed - the fetcher declares no credentials (:74).

One POST to the v2 timeseries endpoint with a JSON body carrying the series list plus startyear and endyear (utils/helpers.py:63-81), fanned out per symbol chunk and per year window (models/series.py:111-131) and gathered (:106); the latest flag is converted from string to boolean and observations re-keyed (utils/helpers.py:139). NO LABEL FOR: request chunking against the 50-series and 20-year API caps (providers/bls/openbb_bls/models/series.py:124-130).

Report, frequency and country generate the flow-id map (:83-87) and every id is fetched concurrently (:90-98); each response is reduced to a period-to-observation dict keyed by the report column name (:93) and the per-series dicts are assembled into rows in the tail (:100). The transport of get_series_data (utils/ecb_helpers.py) was not opened, so the endpoint count reflects the per-series fan-out rather than distinct URLs.

Single GET of the daily euro fx reference XML (:49-50) parsed with xmltodict (:56) and read down the envelope/Cube/Cube/Cube path (:57); the Cube list is exploded into a currency-to-rate dict and assembled as one row with the base currency pinned (:58-61). NO LABEL FOR: xml attribute extraction on at-prefixed keys (providers/ecb/openbb_ecb/models/currency_reference_rates.py:58).

Rating and curve type select a vendored id roster (:76-80) and one GET per maturity is issued against the data-detail-api base (:82-84) through an aiohttp SQLiteBackend cache in the user cache directory (:65-68); the observation key path past :84 was not opened, so the SDMX labels rest on the endpoint family rather than a payload I read, and no local fetcher class name is confirmed for this model.
